decisions.key: MCP.ClientTest/test concurrent requests handles multiple concurrent requests
decisions.label: ET-CC
decisions.spec_anchor: schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts:665-666 (DiscoverRequest.method "server/discover")
decisions.question: Do assertions executed inside a shared setup HELPER count as the unit's own assertions for §6? RESOLVED by PM ruling C (26035): yes — ratified Part A (§6, indivisibility) outranks a §9 tie-break, and the tie-break's naming of :353 decided that row's OWN {:error, :timeout} assertion, not inherited ones. The consequence the PM accepted and recorded as a Part A amendment candidate: every test sharing an asserting setup helper becomes a member. ESTABLISHED that this moves exactly these three and nothing else — do_connect/2 has 17 call sites (client_test.exs:146,170,189,210,228,248,274,311,331,346,368,375,390,404,434,445,492) and the other 14 are already ET-CC on their own assertions; see etcc-register.md §7.
decisions.evidence: client_test.exs:465-466 — `assert {:ok, _} = Task.await(t1)` twice. Only the return-tuple SHAPE is asserted; no value on either side of the wire is checked. ESCALATION — this unit's OWN assertions are all SDK-invented values (ET-OUT), but it calls the do_connect/2 helper (client_test.exs:59-80), which contains `assert discover["method"] == "server/discover"` and `assert result.server_info.name == "test-server"`. A test is indivisible, so under §6's any-assertion rule those helper assertions are this test's assertions and would lift it to ET-CC. Labelled ET-OUT here because that is the answer the PM's tie-break (comment 26026) gives for the artefact this unit is ABOUT, and because the alternative makes every test sharing an asserting setup helper an ET-CC member. Provisional; the question is on the row. || PM ruling C (26035): §6 is ratified Part A and a test is indivisible, so do_connect/2's `assert discover["method"] == "server/discover"` (client_test.exs:62) is this unit's own assertion. It asserts a JSON-RPC request method read off the transport's recorded wire map (gate 2) and schema.ts:665-666 types `method: "server/discover"` (gate 3). falsifiable: yes, MEASURED — mutating %Request{}'s encoder (request.ex:25) reddened this unit on exactly that assertion. mixed: true — the unit's own body asserts an SDK-invented value ({:error, :timeout} / a pending-request notification / concurrent completion) which earns ET-OUT, and §6 takes the highest.

adjudication.outcome: overturned: provisional ET-OUT -> ET-CC, mixed

decisions.question:
Does gate 2 pass for the output of a PUBLIC encode boundary this SDK's own transports never route through? §2 admits "the output of the public encode/decode boundary that produces one", and Protocol.encode!/1 literally returns a JSON-RPC message string that a consumer puts on the wire. But §2.1's counterfactual bites if "this wire behaviour" is read as "the message THIS SDK emits", because MEASURED at 94f4d2a: `MCP.Protocol.encode/1` and `encode!/1` have ZERO lib/ call sites — established ALIAS-AWARE, not by a qualified-name grep: the four bare `encode(...)` call sites in lib/ (client.ex:839/:864, connection.ex:203, subscriptions.ex:258, subscription.ex:91) each resolve to that module's OWN `defp encode(struct), do: Jason.decode!(Jason.encode!(struct))` at client.ex:868, connection.ex:208, subscriptions.ex:307 and subscription.ex:158. *** ROUND-3 CORRECTION (F3, CODE_REVIEWER at comment 26045; PM ruled it BLOCKING at 26047). Round 1's third conjunct — 'and `MCP.Protocol.Messages.Response` is used NOWHERE in lib/' — is FALSE and is WITHDRAWN FROM THIS ROW, not merely from the prose. *** `Response` is aliased at protocol.ex:7, client.ex:98 and connection.ex:35, constructed at protocol.ex:98 and pattern-matched at connection.ex:112 and client.ex:363,415,435,449,463,538,563,582,597,640,656,665 — every one of them INBOUND. The narrower claim that survives is the one this label rests on: `Response.success/2` and `Response.error/2` have ZERO lib/ call sites (`grep -rnE 'Response\.(success|error|new)\(' lib/` returns 0, re-run at this tip), no lib/ path re-encodes a %Response{}, and mutating %Response{}'s defimpl reddens 2 of 979, both in MCP.ProtocolTest. See S7-16. Also: the only MCP.Protocol function on a live path is decode_message/1 (client.ex:362, connection.ex:103, plug.ex:324). The SDK's own responses are built by hand at dispatch.ex:723-729 and plug.ex send_json_error. Provisional ET-CC on the reading that §2.1 is scoped to the behaviour the ASSERTION names. Identical question on error_test.exs:84 and :94; one answer settles all nine rows.

ADJUDICATED by PM ruling A (26034): an assertion on the output of a public encode/decode boundary that NO lib/ call site routes to a transport fails gate 2. Established per row at 2026-08-23 by encoder mutation over the full 979-unit suite; see `evidence`. decisions.key: MCP.Server.DispatchTest/test MC-1 depth — the per-request context reaches all eight identity-capable callbacks
decisions.label: ET-OUT
decisions.question: GATE-3 BOUNDARY, escalated because it decides a family of 7 rows and I can argue it both ways. These units assert an identity STRING that the SDK threaded from ToolContext.identity into a handler and out through a spec-defined response envelope. Gate 2 passes: the artefact read is the decoded server response and the test would raise or fail if `content`/`text`/`messages`/`resourceTemplates` were misspelled. PROVISIONAL: ET-OUT at gate 3, on §10 category 6 — 'reaches the wire, but the spec does not govern the value being exercised. The one that looks most like a member and is not.' No 2026-07-28 requirement governs what a tool returns, nor says that a model-supplied `identity` argument must not become the caller principal; that rule is CLAUDE.md critical rule 6, sourced from this project's identity-threading design spec, not from the pinned revision. The nearest spec text is schema.ts:85-88 (clientInfo 'is not verified by the protocol', servers 'SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions'), which is about clientInfo in _meta and not about tool arguments — naming it would be the AC7 error of claiming a bound that does not hold. THE OTHER READING: the envelope field names ARE load-bearing for whether these tests pass, and §3 only requires that the sweeper can PRODUCE an anchor — CallToolResult.content (schema.ts:1813), TextContent.text (:2316-2320), GetPromptResult.messages, ListResourceTemplatesResult.resourceTemplates (:1169-1171) are all nameable. On that reading every one of these is ET-CC with mixed: true. I take the first reading because §12's second inherited warning says a proxy for a gate is not the gate, and the envelope is how the value travelled rather than what the unit claims.

decisions.key: MCP.Server.SubscriptionsDispatchTest/test open-time authorization via the honoured subset identity reaches handle_listen/3 from the context, never from params
decisions.label: ET-OUT
decisions.question: GATE-3 BOUNDARY, escalated because it decides a family of 7 rows and I can argue it both ways. These units assert an identity STRING that the SDK threaded from ToolContext.identity into a handler and out through a spec-defined response envelope. Gate 2 passes: the artefact read is the decoded server response and the test would raise or fail if `content`/`text`/`messages`/`resourceTemplates` were misspelled. PROVISIONAL: ET-OUT at gate 3, on §10 category 6 — 'reaches the wire, but the spec does not govern the value being exercised. The one that looks most like a member and is not.' No 2026-07-28 requirement governs what a tool returns, nor says that a model-supplied `identity` argument must not become the caller principal; that rule is CLAUDE.md critical rule 6, sourced from this project's identity-threading design spec, not from the pinned revision. The nearest spec text is schema.ts:85-88 (clientInfo 'is not verified by the protocol', servers 'SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions'), which is about clientInfo in _meta and not about tool arguments — naming it would be the AC7 error of claiming a bound that does not hold. THE OTHER READING: the envelope field names ARE load-bearing for whether these tests pass, and §3 only requires that the sweeper can PRODUCE an anchor — CallToolResult.content (schema.ts:1813), TextContent.text (:2316-2320), GetPromptResult.messages, ListResourceTemplatesResult.resourceTemplates (:1169-1171) are all nameable. On that reading every one of these is ET-CC with mixed: true. I take the first reading because §12's second inherited warning says a proxy for a gate is not the gate, and the envelope is how the value travelled rather than what the unit claims.
decisions.evidence: subscriptions_dispatch_test.exs:528-529 — a params-borne identity spoof does not reach `handle_listen/3`; the handler is told "alice", from the context. Same family as dispatch_test.exs:41/:54/:64 — see the escalation question. Here the artefact is additionally a test-handler message rather than a wire value, so gate 2 is doubtful too.

adjudication.outcome: upheld as ruled: gate 3 fails on §10 category 6; no change

decisions.label: ET-OUT
decisions.evidence: stdio_test.exs:153 — `assert_receive {:mcp_transport_closed, _reason}`. The asserted artefact is an SDK-invented BEAM message announcing subprocess exit; it has no wire counterpart (a closed pipe is the absence of bytes, not a value). ET-ADJ is unreachable: the consumers of `:mcp_transport_closed` (client.ex's handle_info) fail pending requests locally and produce nothing on any wire.

decisions.key: MCP.Transport.StreamableHTTP.ACTest/test AC1 — static handler_opts identity threads per request
decisions.label: ET-OUT
decisions.question: GATE-3 BOUNDARY, escalated because it decides a family of 7 rows and I can argue it both ways. These units assert an identity STRING that the SDK threaded from ToolContext.identity into a handler and out through a spec-defined response envelope. Gate 2 passes: the artefact read is the decoded server response and the test would raise or fail if `content`/`text`/`messages`/`resourceTemplates` were misspelled. PROVISIONAL: ET-OUT at gate 3, on §10 category 6 — 'reaches the wire, but the spec does not govern the value being exercised. The one that looks most like a member and is not.' No 2026-07-28 requirement governs what a tool returns, nor says that a model-supplied `identity` argument must not become the caller principal; that rule is CLAUDE.md critical rule 6, sourced from this project's identity-threading design spec, not from the pinned revision. The nearest spec text is schema.ts:85-88 (clientInfo 'is not verified by the protocol', servers 'SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions'), which is about clientInfo in _meta and not about tool arguments — naming it would be the AC7 error of claiming a bound that does not hold. THE OTHER READING: the envelope field names ARE load-bearing for whether these tests pass, and §3 only requires that the sweeper can PRODUCE an anchor — CallToolResult.content (schema.ts:1813), TextContent.text (:2316-2320), GetPromptResult.messages, ListResourceTemplatesResult.resourceTemplates (:1169-1171) are all nameable. On that reading every one of these is ET-CC with mixed: true. I take the first reading because §12's second inherited warning says a proxy for a gate is not the gate, and the envelope is how the value travelled rather than what the unit claims.
decisions.evidence: streamable_http_ac_test.exsstreamable_http_ac_test.exs:104-106 — a STATIC handler_opts identity ("REVIEWER") reaches the tool and comes back as the content text. Driven through the real Streamable HTTP plug, so the HTTP status, headers and decoded response body ARE the wire artefacts (§2 names a transport header or status directly).

adjudication.outcome: upheld as ruled: gate 3 fails on §10 category 6; no change

decisions.key: MCP.Transport.StreamableHTTP.ClientTest/test A6-11: `content-encoding: identity` is tolerated and does NOT error
decisions.label: ET-OUT
decisions.evidence: streamable_http_client_test.exs:112-113 — `content-encoding: identity` is tolerated: `:ok` and the decoded message is delivered to the owner. GATE 2 PASSES on the second assertion — `assert_receive {:mcp_message, %{"result" => %{"ok" => true}}}` reads a decoded JSON-RPC response that crossed a real HTTP connection. GATE 3 FAILS, established by search rather than assumed: `grep -rn "ccept-[Ee]ncoding\|ontent-[Ee]ncoding\|gzip"` over the whole pinned docs/specification/2026-07-28 tree and schema.ts returns ZERO hits. Content coding is governed by RFC 9110 §12.5.3 (a SHOULD) and the SDK's choice here is a security decision against EEF-CVE-2026-49755 (req's decompression is opt-in and unbounded — a decompression-bomb DoS), not an MCP requirement. §10 category 6. decisions.question: GATE-3 BOUNDARY, escalated because it decides a family of 7 rows and I can argue it both ways. These units assert an identity STRING that the SDK threaded from ToolContext.identity into a handler and out through a spec-defined response envelope. Gate 2 passes: the artefact read is the decoded server response and the test would raise or fail if `content`/`text`/`messages`/`resourceTemplates` were misspelled. PROVISIONAL: ET-OUT at gate 3, on §10 category 6 — 'reaches the wire, but the spec does not govern the value being exercised. The one that looks most like a member and is not.' No 2026-07-28 requirement governs what a tool returns, nor says that a model-supplied `identity` argument must not become the caller principal; that rule is CLAUDE.md critical rule 6, sourced from this project's identity-threading design spec, not from the pinned revision. The nearest spec text is schema.ts:85-88 (clientInfo 'is not verified by the protocol', servers 'SHOULD NOT rely on it for security decisions'), which is about clientInfo in _meta and not about tool arguments — naming it would be the AC7 error of claiming a bound that does not hold. THE OTHER READING: the envelope field names ARE load-bearing for whether these tests pass, and §3 only requires that the sweeper can PRODUCE an anchor — CallToolResult.content (schema.ts:1813), TextContent.text (:2316-2320), GetPromptResult.messages, ListResourceTemplatesResult.resourceTemplates (:1169-1171) are all nameable. On that reading every one of these is ET-CC with mixed: true. I take the first reading because §12's second inherited warning says a proxy for a gate is not the gate, and the envelope is how the value travelled rather than what the unit claims.
